subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: What request-scoped no-side-effects contract should OpenClaw expose for global agent tool dry-run across CLI, Gateway or embedded runs, built-in/plugin/client tools, direct tool invocation, and hooks?
rationale: The requested behavior is a user-trusted security/product guarantee, and current source has multiple execution surfaces where a narrow CLI or process-global adapter flag could leave side effects possible.

options.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
options.body: Specify the runtime contract first, then implement an additive CLI/runtime path with coverage for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, direct-invoke, and hook behavior.

options.title: Fold into workflow modes
options.body: Keep this open but defer implementation until Ask, Plan, Modify, or scoped-agent mode defines the shared preview vocabulary and safety guarantees.

options.title: Keep scoped dry-runs only
options.body: Reject a global mode if maintainers decide it is too easily confused with sandboxing, and continue improving command-specific previews instead.

recommendation.title: Design request-scoped core dry-run
recommendation.body: Specify the runtime contract first, then implement an additive CLI/runtime path with coverage for built-in, plugin, client, Gateway, embedded, direct-invoke, and hook behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a product/security-contract decision and this handle appears in older tool-adapter feature history.
